newsitem.title: MEXICO: African elephant born in captivity in Mexico dies.
newsitem.headline: African elephant born in captivity in Mexico dies.

text.p: A baby elephant that was born on New Year's Day, the first African elephant born in captivity in Mexico, died on Friday, zoo officials said.
The unnamed baby elephant was born prematurely and was too small to reach its mother's mammary glands.
It died of heart and lung failure related to gastrointestinal problems because of its premature birth, said La Pastora Park Zoo officials in this northern industrial city.
The baby elephant's brief life was prominently featured in the local media, and was followed by people all over Mexico.

The Education Ministry had sponsored a competition among local school children to name her, and zoo officials had been gearing up for a Jan. 18 debut, when she was to be presented to the public for the first time.
Previously she had only been seen in a snippet of video released by the zoo, showing her romping around her pen.

"We deeply lament her death," state government spokesman Jose Luis Carrillo told reporters on Friday. "This morning we were going to try a blood transfusion with her mother, but lamentably it was too late."
Mexican Radio Red reported that the body would be stuffed and put on display at a museum in Monterrey.

The baby elephant was born weighing just 95 pounds (43 kg) when it should have weighed about 220 pounds (100 kg) and at a height of 28 inches (70 cm) when it should have been about 40 inches (one meter), zoo officials told a news conference.
